program_educational_objectives.description: Practice chemical engineering in traditional and emerging fields.
Excel in advanced studies with a strong foundation laid in undergraduate education.
Exhibit leadership, ethical attitude, communication skills, teamwork in their profession and multidisciplinary skills.
Engage in lifelong learning and continuous professional development.

programme_outcomes.title: Engineering knowledge
programme_outcomes.description: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

programme_outcomes.title: Problem analysis
programme_outcomes.description: Identify, formulate, research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

programme_outcomes.title: Design/development of solutions
programme_outcomes.description: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, and cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

programme_outcomes.title: Investigation of complex problems
programme_outcomes.description: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

programme_outcomes.title: Modern tool usage
programme_outcomes.description: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modelling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of their limitations.

programme_outcomes.title: Engineer and society
programme_outcomes.description: Apply reasoning informed by contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to professional engineering practice.

programme_outcomes.title: Environment and sustainability
programme_outcomes.description: Understand the impact of professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for, sustainable development.

programme_outcomes.title: Ethics
programme_outcomes.description: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.

programme_outcomes.title: Individual and team work
programme_outcomes.description: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.

programme_outcomes.title: Communication
programme_outcomes.description: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, including writing effective reports, making effective presentations, and giving and receiving clear instructions.

programme_outcomes.title: Project management and finance
programme_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one's own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects in multidisciplinary environments.

programme_outcomes.title: Life-long learning
programme_outcomes.description: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

programme_specific_outcomes.description: Apply the principles of chemical engineering to design, analyze, optimize and control chemical processes and systems in various industries.
Develop solutions for complex engineering problems using conventional, modern tools and techniques.
Think individually, communicate effectively, work in teams and assume positions as leaders.

effort_notation.T: Tutorial – 50 min per unit (marked * = optional, can be replaced by self-study)
effort_notation.O: Outside class / self-study – 1 hour per unit

semester_plan.notes: Activity Points minimum 20 required by end of Semester 4.

courses.title: Reaction Engineering and Process Control Lab

semester_plan.notes: Activity Points minimum 40 required by end of Semester 6.

courses.title: Summer Internship
courses.note: Duration decided by the host organisation; minimum 8 weeks during summer vacation of 3rd year

courses.title: Project Part II / Internship / Programme Elective
courses.note: Students choose one: CH4094E Project Part II, CH4092E Internship, or a Programme Elective

courses.title: Project Part III / Internship / Programme Electives
courses.note: Students choose one: CH4095E Project Part III, CH4093E Internship, or Programme Electives. Project Part III preferably done as Internship / Product development / Entrepreneurship / Research project.

institute_core.title: Mathematics I
course_outcomes: CO1: Formulate engineering problems as ODEs and solve them.
CO2: Solve linear ODEs with constant coefficients.
CO3: Find limits, check continuity and differentiability of real valued functions of two variables.
CO4: Test for the convergence of sequences and series.
CO5: Find the Fourier series representing periodic functions.
topics: First order ODEs: existence and uniqueness, methods of solution, orthogonal trajectories
Second order ODEs with constant coefficients: Wronskian, undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, Euler-Cauchy equations
Applications of first and second order ODEs, systems of linear ODEs
Functions of several variables: limit, continuity, partial derivatives, gradient, Lagrange multipliers, Taylor's formula
Parametrised curves in space, arc length, curvature, torsion
Sequences, Cauchy sequence, series, convergence tests, power series, Taylor series
Periodic functions, Fourier series, Fourier integrals, Fourier transforms
references: H. Anton, I. Bivens & S. Davis, Calculus, 10th Edn., Wiley, 2015
G. B. Thomas et al., Thomas' Calculus, 12th Edn., Pearson, 2015
E. Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10th Edn., Wiley, 2015
Apostol, Calculus Vol 1, Wiley, 2014

institute_core.title: Mathematics II
course_outcomes: CO1: Find parametric representation of curves and surfaces and evaluate integrals over them.
CO2: Use Laplace transform to solve differential and integral equations.
CO3: Test consistency of linear equations and solve them.
CO4: Diagonalise symmetric matrices and find the nature of quadratic forms.
topics: Vector fields, divergence, curl, scalar potential, line integrals, Green's theorem
Double and triple integrals, Jacobian, polar/cylindrical/spherical coordinates
Surface integrals, flux, Gauss' divergence theorem, Stokes' theorem
Laplace transform, Dirac delta function, convolution, shifting theorems, solving ODEs and integral equations
System of linear equations, Gauss elimination, LU decomposition, rank, eigenvalues, eigenvectors
Cayley-Hamilton theorem, diagonalisation, quadratic forms, reduction to canonical form
references: E. Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10th Edn., Wiley, 2015
H. Anton et al., Calculus, 10th Edn., Wiley, 2015
P. Dyke, Introduction to Laplace Transforms and Fourier Series, Springer

institute_core.title: Mathematics III
course_outcomes: CO1: Understand series solutions for ordinary differential equations.
CO2: Model physical phenomena through PDEs and apply solution techniques.
CO3: Solve linear and non-linear algebraic equations numerically.
CO4: Understand numerical differentiation and integration.
topics: ODE series solutions: Frobenius method, Legendre equation, Bessel's equation, Sturm-Liouville problems
PDEs of first order: Cauchy problem, Lagrange and Charpit methods
Modelling through PDEs: heat, wave and Laplace equations; Fourier method and integral techniques
Classification of second-order PDEs
Numerical methods: root-finding, iterative methods for linear systems, numerical differentiation and integration
Numerical ODE solutions: initial value problems (Runge-Kutta), boundary value problems (shooting methods)
references: E. Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, Wiley, 9th Edn., 2012
M. D. Raisinghania, Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations, S. Chand, 20th Edn., 2020
M. K. Jain et al., Numerical Methods for Scientific and Engineering Computation, 8th Edn., New Age International, 2022

institute_core.title: Mathematics IV
course_outcomes: CO1: Understand basic concepts of one- and two-dimensional random variables and apply them in engineering.
CO2: Use techniques of statistical inference and their applications.
CO3: Apply regression and correlation for analysing real-life problems.
CO4: Understand sampling distributions and statistical techniques used in engineering and management.
topics: Probability distributions: discrete and continuous random variables, Chebyshev's inequality
Normal, Student's t, Chi-Square and F distributions, transformation of random variables
Jointly distributed random variables, marginal and conditional distributions, bivariate normal distribution
Statistical inference: point and interval estimates, hypothesis testing (means, variances, proportions)
Chi-square test for goodness of fit, contingency tables
Regression: curve fitting, least squares, simple regression, correlation coefficient
Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) for single factor experiments
references: S. Ross, A First Course in Probability, 9th Edn., Pearson, 2014
R. A. Johnson, Miller and Freund's Probability and Statistics for Engineers, 8th Edn., PHI, 2011
D. C. Montgomery & G. C. Runger, Applied Statistics and Probability for Engineers, 7th Edn., 2019

institute_core.title: Chemistry I
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply fundamentals of thermodynamics and photochemistry to real-life engineering problems.
CO2: Utilise principles of inorganic chemistry for innovative applications.
CO3: Apply basics of electrochemistry to advanced technologies.
topics: Thermodynamics: Helmholtz and Gibbs free energy, entropy, Maxwell relations, Van't Hoff equation, chemical potential
Phase diagrams of mixtures: volatile liquids, liquid-liquid, liquid-solid, reaction equilibria
Photochemistry: quantum yield, actinometry, photosensitisation, photodegradation, photocatalysts
Molecular orbital theory: bonding in diatomic molecules, coordination chemistry, crystal field theory
Metal ions in living systems: haemoglobin, myoglobin; organometallics and catalysis
Electrochemistry: ion-solvent and ion-ion interactions, electrolytic conductivity, galvanic cells, electrical double layer
Electroanalytical techniques: potentiometry, polarography, voltammetry, coulometry, amperometry, impedance spectroscopy
references: P. Atkins & J. Paula, Physical Chemistry, 8th Edn., Freeman, 2006
J. E. Huheey et al., Inorganic Chemistry, Pearson India, 2009
J. Bard & L. R. Faulkner, Electrochemical Methods, 2nd Edn., Wiley, 2001

institute_core.title: Physics of Materials
course_outcomes: CO1: Explain fundamentals of quantum mechanics.
CO2: Apply quantum mechanics to electrons in crystals and study band formation in solids.
CO3: Apply quantum mechanics to study electrical properties of solids.
CO4: Explain conductivity in semiconducting materials and influence of dopants.
topics: Quantum mechanics: wave-particle duality, de Broglie waves, uncertainty principle, Schrodinger's wave equation
Applications to free particle and particle in a box
Band theory of solids: Bloch theorem, Kronig-Penney model, E-k diagram, band gap
Electrical conductivity: classical electron theory, Fermi energy and Fermi surface, density of states, effective mass
Semiconductors: intrinsic and extrinsic, carrier concentration, Fermi level, temperature dependence of conductivity
references: Beiser, Concepts of Modern Physics, 6th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2009
K. Krane, Modern Physics, 4th Indian Edn., Wiley, 2021
M. A. Wahab, Solid State Physics, 3rd Edn., Narosa, 2015

institute_core.title: Professional Ethics
course_outcomes: CO1: Develop a clear understanding of human values and use it as the basis for all activities.
CO2: Understand and follow the ethical aspects of the engineering profession.
CO3: Align with the AIChE Code of Ethics in all professional activities.
CO4: Assimilate the elements of Academic Integrity and Honour Codes.
topics: Human values: morals, integrity, work ethic, civic virtue, honesty, commitment, empathy, self-confidence
Ethics in professional context: ethical responsibilities to consumers, safety and risk, IP management, environmental sustainability
AIChE Code of Ethics, academic integrity: honesty, trust, fairness, respect, responsibility, plagiarism
Honour codes and expected ethical standards from stakeholders
references: R. S. Naagarazan, Textbook on Professional Ethics and Human Values, 3rd Edn., New Age International, 2022
A. F. Bainbridge, Ethics for Engineers, CRC Press, 2021
C. E. Harris Jr. et al., Engineering Ethics: Concepts and Cases, Cengage, 6th Edn., 2019
AIChE Code of Ethics, American Institute of Chemical Engineers, New York

institute_core.title: Professional Communication
course_outcomes: CO1: Distinguish the role and purpose of communication at the workplace and for academic purposes.
CO2: Decide strategies and modes for effective communication in a dynamic workplace.
CO3: Combine multiple approaches for successful and ethical information exchange.
CO4: Estimate best communication practices to assist productivity and congeniality.
topics: Listening and reading comprehension: introductions, feedback, public speaking
Vocabulary development, critical reading, understanding text structures
Effective writing: note-making, paragraph writing, official letters, emails, abstract writing
Communication theory, verbal/nonverbal communication, group discussions, presentations, digital communication etiquette
references: N. Bhatnagar, Communicative English for Engineers and Professionals, Dorling Kindersley, 2010
B. A. Garner, HBR Guide to Better Business Writing, Harvard Business Review Press, 2012
S. Kumar & P. Lata, Communication Skills, Oxford University Press, 2015

programme_core.title: Material and Energy Balance
course_outcomes: CO1: Identify areas where Chemical Engineering plays a major role.
CO2: Understand units of measurement and conversions between systems.
CO3: Quantify mass in moles and vice versa.
CO4: Apply equations of state to characterise gas mixtures and humidity.
CO5: Formulate and solve material balance equations for steady-state processes with and without reactions.
CO6: Formulate energy balance in closed and open systems and calculate heat of chemical reactions.
topics: Introduction: chemical engineering applications, unit operations and processes, units and dimensions, mole and concentration concepts
Ideal and real gases, vapour pressure, vapour-liquid equilibrium, humidity and saturation
Material balance: general equation, steady-state processes, recycle, bypass and purge calculations
Material balance with reactions: limiting/excess reactants, fractional and percentage conversion, yield
Energy balance: heat capacity, enthalpy changes, phase transitions, thermochemistry, Hess's law
Orsat analysis, ultimate and proximate analysis of coal, theoretical flame temperature
references: K. V. Narayanan & B. Lakshmikuttyamma, Stoichiometry & Process Calculations, 2nd Edn., PHI, 2016
D. H. Himmelblau, Basic Principles and Calculations in Chemical Engineering, 8th Edn., PHI, 2014
R. M. Felder & R. W. Rousseau, Elementary Principles of Chemical Processes, 3rd Edn., Wiley, 2008

programme_core.title: Elements of Biotechnology
course_outcomes: CO1: Illustrate the scope, significance and types of Biotechnology.
CO2: Describe organisation of living cells and their function.
CO3: Review essentials of biomolecules, molecular biology and genetic engineering.
CO4: Demonstrate applications of biotechnology for energy, environment and value-added products.
topics: Introduction: history, scope, ethics, types (microbial, agricultural, food, medical), metabolic processes
Biochemistry: biomolecules (carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids), central dogma, recombinant DNA technology
Bioproducts: baker's yeast, algae, amino acids, organic acids, antibiotics, bioplastics, enzymes, biosensors, vaccines
Biofuels: bioethanol, biogas; bioremediation for petroleum spills and wastewater treatment
references: C. Ratledge & B. Kristiansen, Basic Biotechnology, 3rd Edn., Cambridge, 2006
W. J. Thieman & M. A. Palladino, Introduction to Biotechnology, 4th Edn., Pearson, 2021
S. C. Bhatia, Textbook of Biotechnology, Atlantic Publishers, 2005

programme_core.title: Chemical Analysis Lab
course_outcomes: CO1: Analyse oil properties.
CO2: Estimate the quality of sugar, soap and soil.
CO3: Evaluate water pollutants quantitatively and qualitatively.
lab_topics: Determination of flash, fire and smoke points
Determination of total organic carbon content
Separation using paper chromatography and TLC
Determination of boiling point range of oils using distillation apparatus
Moisture analysis of oils using Karl Fischer Titrator
references: R. Gopalan et al., Textbook of Engineering Chemistry, 4th Edn., Vikas, 2013
G. H. Jeffery et al., Vogel's Textbook of Quantitative Chemical Analysis, 5th Edn., Longman, 1989
R. B. Baird, Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater, 23rd Edn., APHA, 2017

programme_core.title: Chemistry II
course_outcomes: CO1: Choose suitable separation strategies for identification of molecules.
CO2: Identify appropriate characterisation techniques for molecules and materials.
CO3: Examine fundamental concepts of reaction mechanisms in synthetic chemistry.
topics: Separation techniques: chromatography, retention and separation factors, theoretical plates
Mass spectrometry: ionisation methods, ESI-MS, high-resolution MS, fragmentation processes
Spectroscopic techniques: IR, UV/Vis, NMR (1H and 13C), chemical shifts, Woodward-Fieser rules
X-ray diffraction; structure elucidation of organic molecules
Reaction mechanisms: kinetic vs thermodynamic control, Curtin-Hammett principle
Synthesis of fine chemicals: hydroboration, dihydroxylation, epoxidation, oxidative cleavage
Polymerisation methods: cationic, anionic, radical chain; cross-linking; stereochemistry of polymers
references: C. N. Banwell & E. M. McCash, Fundamentals of Molecular Spectroscopy, 5th Edn., McGraw Hill, 2013
R. M. Silverstein et al., Spectrometric Identification of Organic Compounds, 7th Edn., Wiley, 2005
F. A. Carey & R. J. Sundberg, Advanced Organic Chemistry Parts A & B, 5th Edn., Springer, 2008

programme_core.title: Introduction to Computing
course_outcomes: CO1: Understand basic programming principles needed for engineers.
CO2: Create algorithms and flowcharts for a computer program.
CO3: Compile and run programs in computers with accuracy.
CO4: Apply programming skills to solve numerical schemes used in Chemical Engineering.
topics: Basic computer fundamentals: CPU, ALU, registers, memory, number systems, fixed and floating-point numbers
C++ basics: algorithms, flowcharts, input/output, operators, control structures, file I/O, preprocessor directives
Arrays and functions: void and value-returning functions, recursion, function overloading, pointers, dynamic arrays
Object-oriented programming: classes, objects
Numerical methods: Gaussian elimination, Thomas algorithm, Jacobi/Gauss-Seidel methods, bisection, Newton-Raphson
Numerical interpolation, differentiation and integration: difference tables, trapezoidal rule, Simpson's rule
references: E. Balaguruswamy, Object Oriented Programming with C++, 8th Edn., Tata McGraw Hill, 2020
S. S. Sastry, Introductory Methods of Numerical Analysis, 5th Edn., PHI, 2012
H. M. Dietel & P. J. Dietel, C++ How to Program, 10th Edn., Prentice Hall, 2016

programme_core.title: Process Fluid Mechanics
course_outcomes: CO1: Understand the basic laws and equations governing fluid flows.
CO2: Calculate head losses in pipe flows and chemical engineering systems.
CO3: Choose the right fluid measurement devices and pumps for required applications.
topics: Fluid concepts: Newtonian/non-Newtonian fluids, fluid kinematics, vorticity, Reynolds transport theorem
Continuity equation, Navier-Stokes equations, momentum and energy balance
Internal and external flow: boundary layer theory, Bernoulli's equation, pipe flow, head losses
Flow past immersed bodies, packed beds, fluidisation
Fluid machinery: dimensional analysis, flow meters (venturi, orifice, pitot), positive displacement, centrifugal pumps, NPSH
references: W. L. McCabe, J. C. Smith & P. Harriott, Unit Operations of Chemical Engineering, 7th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2017
Y. A. Cengel & J. M. Cimbala, Fluid Mechanics, 4th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2019
N. H. De Nevers, Fluid Mechanics for Chemical Engineers, 3rd Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2004

programme_core.title: Mechanical Operations
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply basic principles of particle characterisation in processes involving solids.
CO2: Evaluate crushing efficiency of different size reduction equipment using crushing laws.
CO3: Analyse various mixing processes and calculate power requirements.
CO4: Select appropriate equipment for particle separation.
topics: Particle characterisation: screen series, particle size analysis, properties of particulate masses
Size reduction: Rittinger's, Kick's and Bond's laws; crushers, grinders, ultrafine grinders; screening
Filtration: cake filtration theory, constant pressure/rate filtration, centrifugal filtration
Sedimentation: gravity settling, batch sedimentation, centrifugal settling, cyclone separation
Other separations: magnetic, electrostatic, froth flotation, jigging
Mixing: agitation equipment, power consumption in agitated vessels, solid/paste mixing
Conveying and storage: bins, silos, hoppers
references: W. L. McCabe, J. C. Smith & P. Harriott, Unit Operations of Chemical Engineering, 7th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2022
J. M. Coulson & J. F. Richardson, Chemical Engineering Vol. II, 5th Edn., Butterworth-Heinemann, 2002
L. Svarovsky, Solid-Liquid Separation, 4th Edn., Butterworth-Heinemann, 2000

programme_core.title: Process Heat Transfer
course_outcomes: CO1: Identify different modes of heat transfer and calculate the rate of heat transfer.
CO2: Apply concepts of 1D steady and unsteady state conduction heat transfer.
CO3: Distinguish between forced and free convection and calculate heat transfer coefficients.
CO4: Understand phase change mechanisms in boiling and condensation.
CO5: Calculate area, number of tubes, heat duty of heat exchangers and evaporators.
CO6: Calculate radiation heat transfer between surfaces and understand view factors.
topics: Conduction: Fourier's law, steady-state through walls, cylinders, spheres, extended surfaces, unsteady state
Convection: thermal boundary layers, dimensional analysis, Reynolds/Prandtl/Colburn analogies, heat transfer coefficients
Boiling and condensation: Nusselt equations for film condensation, pool boiling, critical flux
Heat exchangers: LMTD, overall heat transfer coefficient, single/multi-pass, plate heat exchangers, design
Evaporation: single and multiple effect evaporators
Radiation: emissive power, Stefan-Boltzmann law, view factors, radiation between surfaces
references: J. M. Coulson & J. F. Richardson, Chemical Engineering Vol. 1, 6th Edn., Butterworth-Heinemann, 1999
D. Q. Kern, Process Heat Transfer, McGraw Hill, 2001
F. P. Incropera et al., Incropera's Principles of Heat and Mass Transfer, 8th Edn., Wiley, 2017

programme_core.title: Materials Science
course_outcomes: CO1: Classify atomic structures and bonding in materials.
CO2: Interpret characterisation techniques and imperfections in crystalline materials.
CO3: Identify phases, properties and understand phase diagrams of metals.
CO4: Demonstrate different failure mechanisms (deformation, dislocation, fracture) of materials.
CO5: Choose materials, properties, and processing techniques for engineering applications.
topics: Structure of materials: bonding in metals/polymers/ceramics, XRD theory and application, imperfections
Mechanical properties: elastic/plastic deformation, dislocation mechanisms, fatigue, creep
Binary phase diagrams and phase transformations
Composites, corrosion, electronic/thermal/magnetic/optical material properties
Engineering design of materials and material selection
references: Callister, Materials Science and Engineering: An Introduction, 10th Edn., Wiley, 2020
J. F. Shackelford, Introduction to Materials Science for Engineers, 8th Edn., Pearson, 2015
V. Raghavan, Material Science and Engineering, 6th Edn., PHI, 1996

programme_core.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply laws of thermodynamics to various systems and thermodynamic cycles.
CO2: Calculate thermodynamic properties of pure and multi-component systems.
CO3: Analyse phase equilibria of various thermodynamic systems.
CO4: Interpret chemical reaction equilibria for homogeneous and heterogeneous systems.
topics: Laws of thermodynamics: first, second and third law; Carnot, Rankine and refrigeration cycles; entropy balance
PVT behaviour of pure fluids: equations of state, generalized correlations
Solution thermodynamics: chemical potential, fugacity, activity coefficient models, excess properties
Mixing processes: property changes and heat effects of mixing
Phase equilibrium: VLE (Raoult's law, modified Raoult's law, Henry's law), LLE, SLE, VLLE
Chemical reaction equilibria: equilibrium constant, effect of temperature and composition, multireaction equilibria
references: J. M. Smith, H. C. Van Ness & M. M. Abbott, Introduction to Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics, 8th Edn., McGraw Hill, 2018
S. I. Sandler, Chemical, Biochemical and Engineering Thermodynamics, 5th Edn., Wiley India, 2017
Y. A. Cengel & M. A. Boles, Thermodynamics: An Engineering Approach, 8th Edn., McGraw Hill, 2015

programme_core.title: Fluid and Particle Mechanics Lab
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply scientific knowledge in carrying out experiments, collecting data and handling equipment.
CO2: Analyse data, perform calculations and interpret results.
CO3: Work in groups and communicate effectively.
CO4: Demonstrate classical experiments in fluid mechanics and hydraulic machinery.
CO5: Analyse performance of size reduction equipment and separation techniques.
lab_topics: Packed bed and fluidised bed setup
Major and minor losses in pipe fittings and pipelines
Size reduction equipment: jaw crusher, ball mill, roll crusher, pulveriser
Filtration equipment: leaf filter, plate and frame filter press

programme_core.title: Chemical Reaction Engineering
course_outcomes: CO1: Predict the mechanism of homogeneous reactions and calculate rate and temperature dependency.
CO2: Design ideal flow reactors for single reactions under isothermal conditions.
CO3: Design ideal flow reactors for multiple reactions under isothermal conditions.
CO4: Design ideal flow reactors under non-isothermal conditions.
CO5: Determine RTDs for non-ideal flow.
topics: Kinetics of homogeneous reactions: elementary and non-elementary reactions, Arrhenius law, collision and transition state theories
Batch reactor data analysis: integral and differential methods, half-lives
Isothermal reactor design: batch, CSTR and PFR design equations, multiple reactor systems, recycle and autocatalytic reactions
Design for multiple reactions: series and parallel
Non-isothermal reactor design: energy conservation, batch and CSTR, tubular reactors, optimum temperature profiles
Non-ideal flow: residence time distribution (RTD), C, E, F and I curves
references: H. S. Fogler, Elements of Chemical Reaction Engineering, 5th Edn., PHI, 2016
O. Levenspiel, Chemical Reaction Engineering, 3rd Edn., Wiley, 1996
G. F. Froment & K. B. Bischoff, Chemical Reactor Analysis and Design, 3rd Edn., Wiley, 2010

programme_core.title: Mass Transfer Operations
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply fundamentals of mass transfer to determine diffusion coefficient, mass transfer coefficient and rates.
CO2: Apply thermodynamic equilibrium and operating lines to solve absorption, distillation, extraction and drying problems.
CO3: Design absorption, distillation, extraction and drying equipment.
topics: Molecular diffusion in gases, liquids and solids; diffusivity measurement and prediction; eddy diffusion
Mass transfer theories, mass transfer coefficients, interphase mass transfer, overall coefficients
Gas-liquid operations: co-current, counter-current and crosscurrent processes, cascade and stage efficiencies
Gas absorption: absorption factor, tray and packed tower absorbers, HETP, HTU, NTU calculations
Distillation: batch, flash, differential, steam, continuous fractionation; McCabe-Thiele and Ponchon-Savarit methods
Liquid-liquid extraction: single and multistage, triangular and Ponchon-Savarit methods
Drying: theory, drying curves, batch and continuous dryer design
references: C. J. Geankoplis et al., Transport Processes and Separation Process Principles, 5th Edn., PHI, 2018
W. L. McCabe, J. C. Smith & P. Harriott, Unit Operations of Chemical Engineering, 7th Edn., McGraw Hill, 2017
R. E. Treybal, Mass Transfer Operations, 3rd Edn., McGraw Hill, 2017

programme_core.title: Heat and Mass Transfer Lab
course_outcomes: CO1: Design and conduct experiments on heat and mass transfer equipment.
CO2: Collect and analyse experimental data using statistical principles.
CO3: Identify safety concerns related to experimental processes.
CO4: Write effective reports.
CO5: Work as a member of a team.

programme_core.title: Process Instrumentation and Control
course_outcomes: CO1: Explain specifications, design and selection of measuring sensors.
CO2: Analyse process dynamics and derive system response to various input disturbances.
CO3: Describe feedback control and analyse open and closed-loop responses and stability.
CO4: Design P, PI and PID type control systems.
CO5: Enhance feedback control with cascade, feed-forward and ratio control strategies.
topics: Process instrumentation: static and dynamic characteristics, calibration, pressure/temperature/flow measurement
Control valves: construction, sizing, inherent and effective characteristics
Process dynamics: Laplace transforms, transfer functions, block diagrams, linearisation
First and second order system responses: step, impulse, sinusoidal; transportation lag
Control system design: P, PI, PID and on-off controllers, stability, Bode and Nyquist plots
Gain and phase margins, Ziegler-Nichols and Cohen-Coon tuning rules
Advanced strategies: cascade control, feed-forward control, ratio control
references: D. R. Coughanowr & S. E. LeBlanc, Process System Analysis and Control, 3rd Edn., McGraw Hill, 2017
D. E. Seborg et al., Process Dynamics and Control, 4th Edn., Wiley, 2016
B. W. Bequette, Process Control: Modelling, Design and Simulation, 2nd Edn., Pearson, 2023

programme_core.title: Chemical Technology
course_outcomes: CO1: Differentiate unit operations and unit processes of chemical process industries.
CO2: Acquire production process knowledge of chemical and allied process industries.
CO3: Identify product yields, by-products, waste generation and engineering problems.
CO4: Implement new technologies, improve process yields, and minimise waste.
topics: Basic chemical industries: chloro-alkali (caustic soda, chlorine, HCl, bleaching powder, soda ash), sulphuric acid (SCSA, DCDA), cement, paints
Nitrogen, fertilizer, soap and oil industries: ammonia, urea, nitric acid, NPK fertilisers, soaps, detergents, oils/fats processing
Natural industries: pulp, paper, fermentation, industrial alcohol
Fuel and petrochemical industry: industrial gases, methanol, isopropanol, phenol, polyethylene, polypropylene, nylon
Pharmaceutical industry: tablet formulation, granulation, packaging
references: G. T. Austin, Shreve's Chemical Process Industries, 5th Edn., McGraw Hill, 1985
R. G. Rao & M. Sittig, Dryden's Outlines of Chemical Technology, 3rd Edn., Affiliated East-West Publishers, 1997
J. R. Wagner, A Handbook of Chemical Technology, Legare Street Press, 2022

programme_core.title: Reaction Engineering and Process Control Lab
course_outcomes: CO1: Determine kinetic parameters of a reaction in various ideal reactors.
CO2: Assess parameters characterising non-ideal reactors.
CO3: Determine dynamic response of first and second order systems to different forcing functions.
CO4: Determine and compare response of different controller types and their tuning.
CO5: Apply advanced control strategies like cascade control.
lab_topics: Batch reactor: constant volume, isothermal, adiabatic, semi-batch kinetics
Residence time distribution in packed bed reactor
Step response of first and second order systems
Step response of non-interacting and interacting first order systems
Level control trainer and cascade control trainer

programme_core.title: Chemical Process Equipment Design
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply chemical engineering knowledge in design of process equipment.
CO2: Design mechanical aspects of process equipment.
CO3: Design heat and mass transfer equipment for process industries.
CO4: Design reactors and storage vessels.
topics: Mechanical design of vessels: pressure vessels, tall vessels, heads/closures, flange design, supports (skirt, lug, saddle)
Process design of heat transfer equipment: double pipe and shell-and-tube heat exchangers, condensers, evaporators
Storage, agitated and reaction vessel design
Process design of mass transfer equipment: tray and packed distillation/absorption columns
Combined mass and heat transfer equipment: dryers and cooling towers
references: B. C. Bhattacharya, Introduction to Chemical Equipment Design — Mechanical Aspects, CBS Publishers, 1985
L. E. Brownell & E. H. Young, Process Equipment Design, Wiley Eastern, 1968
R. H. Perry & D. W. Green, Chemical Engineers Handbook, 8th Edn., McGraw Hill, 2007

programme_core.title: Transport Phenomena
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply shell balance and Navier-Stokes equation for 1D momentum transport problems.
CO2: Apply shell energy balance and equations of change for non-isothermal energy transport.
CO3: Apply shell mass balance and equations of change for multicomponent mass transport.
topics: Momentum transport: shell momentum balance, velocity profiles, Navier-Stokes equations, dimensional analysis, non-Newtonian fluids, boundary layer concepts
Energy transport: thermal conductivity, shell energy balance, temperature profiles, equations of change for non-isothermal systems, transient conduction
Mass transport: diffusivity, shell mass balance, concentration profiles, equations of change for multicomponent systems
Analogies between heat, mass and momentum transfer, similarity parameters, coupled transport problems
references: R. B. Bird, W. E. Stewart & E. W. Lightfoot, Transport Phenomena, 2nd Edn., Wiley, 2018
J. R. Wilty et al., Fundamentals of Momentum, Heat and Mass Transfer, 5th Edn., Wiley, 2010
C. J. Geankoplis, Transport Processes and Separation Processes Principles, 4th Edn., Pearson, 2018

programme_core.title: Project Part I
course_outcomes: CO1: Work in a team and identify a problem for project work.
CO2: Review and evaluate the available literature on the chosen problem.
CO3: Formulate the methodology to solve the identified problem.
CO4: Apply the principles, tools and techniques to solve the problem.
CO5: Demonstrate written and oral presentation skills.
programme_core.description: Design, experiment or computation-based group project (3–4 students) on any Chemical Engineering topic. Assessed twice per semester (mid-semester and end-semester) by a faculty committee. Groups submit a final signed report kept in the departmental library.

programme_core.title: Summer Internship
course_outcomes: CO1: Provide real-world experience and enable correlation of classroom learning with industrial applications.
CO2: Develop practical engineering skills.
CO3: Help students discover their own interests in Chemical Engineering.
CO4: Inculcate research attitude among students.
programme_core.description: Minimum 8-week industrial training/internship during the summer vacation of B.Tech. 3rd year. Academic internship at IISc/IITs/NITs/CSIR Labs or reputed universities abroad is also allowed. Students submit a comprehensive report and present to a Summer Internship Evaluation Committee. Duration decided by the host organisation.

programme_core.title: Project Part II
course_outcomes: CO1: Work in a team and select a problem for project work.
CO2: Review and evaluate the available literature on the chosen problem.
CO3: Formulate the methodology to solve the identified problem.
CO4: Apply the principles, tools and techniques to solve the problem.
CO5: Develop concept of technical and thesis writing.
programme_core.description: Continuation of Project Part I (Semester VI) or a new topic. Individual or team work. Assessed twice per semester by a faculty committee. Groups submit a completed signed project report.

programme_core.title: Project Part III
course_outcomes: CO1: Work in a team and select a problem for project work.
CO2: Review and evaluate available literature on the chosen problem.
CO3: Formulate the methodology to solve the identified problem.
CO4: Apply principles, tools and techniques to solve the problem.
CO5: Develop concept of technical and thesis writing.
programme_core.description: Continuation of Project Part II. Preferably done as Internship / Product development / Entrepreneurship / Research project. Students complete the work, present before the committee, and are expected to submit and communicate scientific papers to national/international conferences or journals.

energy_and_environmental_engineering.title: Environment Impact Assessment and Clean Technology

selected_elective_syllabi.title: Energy Technology
course_outcomes: CO1: Understand present and future energy challenges in society.
CO2: Describe principles and technologies for harnessing energy from renewable sources.
CO3: Perform energy audits and process integration of unit operations.
CO4: Compare efficiencies of various conventional power plants.
CO5: Classify energy storage and conversion devices.
topics: Conventional energy resources: world and Indian energy consumption, thermal, hydel and nuclear power plants, fluidised bed combustion
Energy conservation: energy audit, pinch technology, process integration
Solar energy: flat plate and focusing collectors, water heating, cooling, distillation, solar ponds, solar thermal power
Wind energy: types of windmills, rotors, wind electric power generation
Ocean and geothermal energy: wave, thermal and tidal energy conversion
Biomass energy: combustion, gasification, pyrolysis, biogas, ethanol
Fuel cells: alkaline, phosphoric acid, molten carbonate, solid oxide, solid polymer electrolyte types
Energy storage: thermal, chemical, mechanical and electrical storage
references: John Twidell & Tony Weir, Renewable Energy Resources, 4th Edn., Taylor & Francis, 2021
Robin Smith, Chemical Process Design and Integration, Wiley, 2005
Aldo V. da Rosa, Fundamentals of Renewable Energy Processes, 4th Edn., Elsevier, 2021

selected_elective_syllabi.title: Polymer Technology
course_outcomes: CO1: Understand basic classifications of polymers, types and kinetics of polymerisation.
CO2: Explain uses and preparations of various polymers.
CO3: Analyse various polymerisation techniques.
CO4: Explain polymer flow properties.
CO5: Illustrate techniques to determine molecular weight of polymers.
CO6: Describe polymer processing techniques and additives.
topics: Polymer chemistry: addition, step and copolymerisation; kinetics; bulk, solution, suspension and emulsion polymerisation techniques
Industrial polymers: thermoplastics (PE, PP, PVC, PS, PMMA, polycarbonates), thermosets (PF, UF, polyester, epoxy, polyurethane)
Molecular weight: number average, weight average, viscosity average; determination by osmometry, light scattering, viscometry, GPC
Rheology: viscous flow, rubber elasticity, viscoelasticity, Maxwell and Voigt elements, stress relaxation, creep, melt flow index
Polymer additives: plasticisers, colourants, heat stabilisers, antioxidants, flame retardants
Processing methods: injection moulding, compression moulding, calendaring, blow moulding, extrusion, thermoforming, spinning
references: J. R. Fried, Polymer Science and Technology, PHI Eastern Economy Edition, 2000
F. W. Billmeyer, Textbook of Polymer Science, Wiley Interscience, 1984
V. R. Gowarikar et al., Polymer Science, Wiley Eastern, 1988

selected_elective_syllabi.title: Ceramic Technology
course_outcomes: CO1: Illustrate importance, properties and applications of ceramic materials.
CO2: Understand synthesis and characterisation of ceramic materials.
CO3: Familiarise with process techniques based on reactions.
CO4: Explain the importance of glass, refractories, cement and concrete.
topics: Introduction to ceramics: classification (traditional, advanced, glass, refractories, cements), mechanical/thermal/optical/magnetic/electrical properties
Processing: size reduction, filtration, mixing, sintering, hot pressing, tape casting, sol-gel, CVD, PECVD, SHS
Property testing: porosity, hardness, density, thermal conductivity, creep
Glass: formation, structure, raw materials, annealing, glass ceramics
Refractories: classification, properties, uses in glass/ceramic industries, special refractories (cermets, ceramic fibres)
Cement and concrete: composition, manufacturing, testing and quality control
references: K. K. Chawla, Ceramic Matrix Composites, 2nd Edn., Kluwer, 2003
B. S. Mitchell, Introduction to Materials Engineering and Science, Wiley, 2004
L. H. Van Vlack, Elements of Material Science and Engineering, 6th Edn., Addison Wesley, 1989

selected_elective_syllabi.title: Fertilizer Technology
course_outcomes: CO1: Classify fertilisers based on their mechanism to improve soil productivity.
CO2: Describe production methods and applications of nitrogenous, potash and combination fertilisers.
CO3: Explain significance and production of biofertilisers.
CO4: Identify engineering and sustainability issues associated with fertiliser manufacturing.
topics: Introduction: soil nutrients (primary, secondary, micronutrients), classification of fertilisers, liming, soil acidity and salinity
Nitrogen: soil organic nitrogen, biological nitrogen fixation, ammonia and urea production, N use efficiency
Phosphorus: phosphate fixation, triple superphosphate production
Potassium: potassium chloride and sulphate production
Mixed fertilisers: MAP, DAP, nitrophosphate, NPK; environmental impact
Biofertilisers: microbial biofertilisers, compost, organic farming, humus, integrated nutrient management
references: J. F. Power & R. Prasad, Soil Fertility Management for Sustainable Agriculture, CRC Press, 1997
S. G. Borkar, Microbes as Biofertilizers and their Production Technology, Woodhead Publishing, 2015
Havlin et al., Soil Fertility and Fertilizers, 8th Edn., Pearson Education India, 2016

selected_elective_syllabi.title: Human Resource Management
course_outcomes: CO1: Identify key terms, theories and practices within HRM.
CO2: Develop employability skills for personnel management.
CO3: Analyse, manage and problem-solve challenges in collective bargaining.
CO4: Solve human resource challenges and industrial conflict resolution.
topics: HR development: manpower planning, recruitment, selection, induction, training, career planning
Job design and motivation: job description, analysis, evaluation, performance appraisal, compensation planning
Laws and rules governing employee benefits and welfare
Industrial relations: discipline, retrenchment, grievance handling, trade unionism, collective bargaining, industrial democracy
references: K. Aswathappa & S. Dash, Human Resource Management, 9th Edn., McGraw Hill, 2021
T. V. Rao & D. F. Pereira, Recent Experiences in Human Resources Development, Oxford & IBH, 1989
P. C. Tripathi, Personnel Management and Industrial Relations, S. Chand, 2013

selected_elective_syllabi.title: Waste to Energy Conversion
course_outcomes: CO1: Classify and characterise waste based on composition and describe government regulations.
CO2: Apply concepts of conversion technologies for zero waste and energy production.
CO3: Apply concepts of refinery for production of value-added chemicals from waste.
topics: Waste availability and characterisation: MSW, plastic waste, biomass, process industry waste; barriers in conversion
Thermochemical conversion: incineration, pyrolysis, gasification; products (pyrolysis oil, biochar, syngas); optimisation
Latest processes: microbial conversion, solar thermal, plasma technology
Biochemical conversion: anaerobic digestion, fermentation, biogas, energy efficiency improvement
Integrated refinery: techno-economic evaluation, life-cycle assessment
references: N. Klinghoffer & M. Castaldi, Waste to Energy Conversion Technology, Woodhead, 2013
C. M. Hussain et al., Waste-to-Energy Approaches Towards Zero Waste, Elsevier, 2021
L. Branchini, Waste-to-Energy: Advanced Cycles and New Design Concepts, Springer, 2015

selected_elective_syllabi.title: Mathematical Methods in Chemical Engineering
course_outcomes: CO1: Develop skills to numerically solve linear and non-linear algebraic equations.
CO2: Apply appropriate numerical methods to solve ODEs.
CO3: Implement appropriate numerical methods to solve PDEs.
CO4: Select appropriate numerical techniques and solve chemical engineering problems using coding languages.
topics: Linear systems: Cramer's rule, Gaussian elimination, LU decomposition, sparse systems, Jacobi/Gauss-Seidel/relaxation methods
Non-linear equations: bisection, Regula-Falsi, Newton-Raphson, Quasi-Newton for single and multi-variable problems
ODE solution: explicit/implicit/predictor-corrector methods, Runge-Kutta, stiffness, shooting methods, finite differences, finite elements
PDE solution: classification, method of lines, Crank-Nicolson, Galerkin FEM, orthogonal collocation; solved using MATLAB
references: S. C. Chapra & R. P. Canale, Numerical Methods for Engineers, 7th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2015
S. Pushpavanam, Mathematical Methods in Chemical Engineering, PHI, 2004
R. G. Rice & D. D. Do, Applied Mathematics and Modelling for Chemical Engineers, Wiley, 1995
